definitions.explanation: In baseball, a player who bats in place of the pitcher in the lineup but does not play a defensive position. The rule is used in Japan's Pacific League and in Major League Baseball. Often abbreviated DH (from the English 'designated hitter').

examples.japanese: ⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{指名打者|しめいだしゃ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{誰|だれ}→誰：00534_dare⟧です⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{指名打者|しめいだしゃ}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{先発|せんぱつ}→先発：17735_senpatsu⟧⟦{出場|しゅつじょう}した→出場する：20348_shutsujousuru⟧。
examples.english: He started the game as the designated hitter.

examples.japanese: パ・リーグ⟦では→では：02945_deha⟧⟦{投手|とうしゅ}→投手：06563_toushu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{代|か}わり→代わり：01296_kawari⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{指名打者|しめいだしゃ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{打席|だせき}→打席：06542_daseki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧。
examples.english: In the Pacific League, the designated hitter bats in place of the pitcher.

notes:
Compound of ⟦{指名|しめい}→指名：12868_shimei⟧ ('designation; nomination') and ⟦{打者|だしゃ}→打者：06564_dasha⟧ ('batter'). The Japanese baseball term for 'designated hitter'.

USAGE:
- The DH rule applies in Japan's Pacific League (パ・リーグ) but not traditionally in the Central League (セ・リーグ), though interleague rules vary.
- In practice, the English abbreviation DH is used widely in Japanese sports media and scoreboards.
- The designated hitter only bats; they do not take the field defensively.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {指名打者|しめいだしゃ}⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧: the designated-hitter rule/system
- {指名打者|しめいだしゃ}⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{出場|しゅつじょう}する→出場する：20348_shutsujousuru⟧: to start/play as the DH
- {指名打者|しめいだしゃ}⟦{解除|かいじょ}→解除：05762_kaijo⟧: removal of the DH (when the DH enters the field)
- ⟦{専門|せんもん}→専門：01251_senmon⟧{指名打者|しめいだしゃ}: a full-time DH

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{打者|だしゃ}→打者：06564_dasha⟧: batter — the general term.
- ⟦{代打|だいだ}→代打：19621_daida⟧: pinch hitter — a substitute batter used for one at-bat only.
- ⟦{投手|とうしゅ}→投手：06563_toushu⟧: pitcher — the position the DH bats in place of.
